resources.string: This wallet has been checked twice, but not yet by an independent human expert. Use it with small amounts only.
Connect to a node of your own
With a TrueNorth node of your own nobody else learns your addresses. The app needs a small setup file for it: where the node is, how to log in, and which addresses to watch, if any.
Make the file on the computer that runs the node and send it to this phone. The password in it is never shown on the screen.
Delete the setup file from the phone after saving
The text is too long to be a setup file.
This is not a setup file.
This setup file is of another kind or version (%1$s).
The node address in the file is not valid.
The node address must start with https://. This app does not send the password over an unencrypted connection.
The user name in the file is missing or not valid.
The password in the file is missing or not valid.
The file names a network this app does not know (%1$s).
The file names no address to watch.
The file names too many addresses. The limit is 20.
An address in the file is not a valid address of that network (%1$s).
The setup file was deleted from the phone.
The setup file could not be deleted from here. Delete it yourself in the Files app: it holds the password in plain text.
The setup was read and the clipboard was cleared.
The file could not be read.

resources.string: The node is still catching up with the network (%1$d of %2$d blocks). The balance below is not complete yet.
Checks on this phone that the key code and its native library give the published answers for the public test phrase: its address and a signed test transaction. It uses no key of yours.
Passed: this phone derives the same address and signs the same transaction as the published vectors, which were checked with TrueNorth Core.
The app forgets the node, its password and the watched addresses. The wallet in this phone and your coins are not touched.
The node cannot be reached. Check the internet connection of this phone. With a node of your own, check also that Tailscale is connected and that the computer with the node is running.
The node refused the user name or the password.
The node does not allow that question. With a node of your own, check its rpcwhitelist line.
The node answered with an error: %1$s
The node works on another network (%1$s) than the setup says.
The node answered with outputs that do not belong to your addresses. Nothing is shown. Check the node.
Something stored in this phone cannot be read or written (%1$s). If the node setup is missing, import it again.
Ask for the fingerprint when the app opens
No wallet in this phone yet
A wallet here can receive and send coins. Its keys are made in this phone and protected by your fingerprint. Keep only amounts you can afford to lose in a phone; larger savings belong on paper.
To bring back a wallet from its recovery words, go to More.
Public descriptor of the receiving addresses. It shows the whole wallet and cannot spend; a TrueNorth Core node can watch the wallet with it.
Remove the wallet from this phone
The recovery words stored in this phone are destroyed. Coins of this wallet can then be reached only with the words you wrote on paper. If you do not have them, the coins are lost for good.
Write these 24 words on paper, in this order. They are the wallet: whoever has them has the coins, and without them a lost phone means lost coins.
Do not photograph them, do not copy them into any app or message, and never type them into a website.
I have written all 24 words on paper
Type these three words from your paper.
Lock the wallet with my fingerprint
Type the 12 or 24 recovery words of an existing wallet, separated by spaces. They will be stored in this phone, protected by your fingerprint. The coins of the wallet are found from the chain.
The wallet was removed from this phone.
Address number %1$d of this wallet. Every address keeps working; a new one for each payer keeps your payments apart.
Compare the address with its source character by character. A payment that has been sent cannot be taken back.
Sign with my fingerprint and send
The node accepted the transaction. Its id:
Your own hash rate can be stored once this phone has a wallet.
Expected figures use the network of the last 120 blocks. Luck compares the blocks found in 24 hours with that expectation.
There is no market price yet. If you type a price per coin, the overview shows what the total would be worth. Nothing is looked up on the internet.

Type the recovery words of a paper address to move its coins. The words are used once and are not stored. After that the paper is no longer safe: move everything, to this wallet or to a new paper address.
Amount for this wallet (empty means everything)
Address for the rest (a new paper address)
This empties the paper address completely.
This is not a valid address of this network.
The amount is not valid. Use a number such as 12.5; the smallest amount is 0.00001.
There is nothing that can be spent now. Coins of a payment that waits for a block, and block rewards younger than 100 blocks, cannot be spent yet.
Not enough coins. With the fee, the most that can be sent is %1$s.
The fee rate is out of bounds.
Too many small coins for one transaction. Send a smaller amount first.
These words belong to another wallet.
These are not valid recovery words. Check the spelling and the order.
The node refused the transaction (%1$s). Nothing was sent.
Without the camera permission a code cannot be read. You can still paste the address.
The code does not hold an address of this network.

About every fifteen minutes the phone asks your node whether a block reward or a payment has arrived, also while the app is closed. It works only while the phone can reach the node, and the phone decides when exactly it runs.
Tell me about a new reward or payment
Notifications are not allowed for this app. Allow them in the settings of the phone.
The node shows the old balance until the payment is in a block. The coins of this payment are not offered for another one meanwhile.
The quickest way to start. The wallet asks a public TrueNorth node what your addresses hold and hands it your signed payments.

A public node sees your addresses and your internet address, and it could show you a false balance or hold a payment back. It cannot take your coins: your keys never leave this phone. For more privacy use a node of your own.
The node did not answer in time. It may be busy. Try again in a moment.
The node is busy. Try again in a moment.
The file that describes the wallet cannot be read (%1$s).
The coins for this payment are tied up in payments that wait for a block. Try again after the next block.

The node did not answer after the payment was handed over, so it is not known whether it went out (id %1$s). Do not pay again now. Refresh when the node can be reached: the payment then shows as waiting for a block, or the app tells you that it did not go through.

Android has destroyed the key that protected the recovery words in this phone. That happens when the screen lock is removed. The words on your paper are now the only way to the coins: remove the wallet here and bring it back from the paper.
This phone still stores the recovery words of an earlier wallet. They are never written over. Rebuild that wallet or remove its words first.
The price must be a plain number such as 0.02.
Recovery words are stored, the wallet file is missing

This phone holds the recovery words of a wallet, but the file that describes the wallet is missing or cannot be read. The wallet can be rebuilt from the stored words with your fingerprint. Its coins are then found again from the chain.
Rebuild the wallet with my fingerprint
A payment of %1$s NORTH that waited for a block is no longer held by the node and is in no block. It did not go through. Look at History before paying again.
Twenty addresses in a row have not been used yet. A wallet brought back from its words looks twenty addresses ahead, so no further one is opened until one of these has been used.
The stored recovery words were removed.
Handed to the node, outcome not known
The node did not confirm that it took this payment. Its coins are kept aside meanwhile. Refresh when the node can be reached.
In payments waiting for a block
One transaction takes at most %1$s coins, and this one is full. Coins left for the next step: %2$d.
One transaction takes at most %1$s coins, and this one is full. Coins left on the paper address: %2$d. The next part is offered right after this one.
%1$s NORTH in block rewards are not ripe yet and stay on the paper address. Keep the paper. Empty the address once more when the last reward has ripened. Blocks until then: about %2$d.
